implementation_statement: POL-02 (P06) was approved 2026-09-17 and covers IT, cloud, and OT, including the low impact BES Cyber Systems. The OT account procedure (SCADA servers, OT domain, jump hosts, relays) is due 2026-11-30.
regulatory_driver: N22-R01 (CIP-003-9 R1 Part 1.2.3); Voluntary benchmark (NIST CSF 2.0; SP 800-82 Rev. 3)

implementation_statement: IT, cloud, OMS, and jump host accounts are provisioned in the identity provider from the HR feed and disabled automatically at termination. OT domain accounts (HMIs, SCADA servers, engineering workstations) are created by the OT engineering team on a manager ticket; HMI operator accounts are named since 2024. Gaps: 3 shared administrator accounts on the SCADA servers have non-expiring passwords and are also used by the SCADA vendor (gap 5); OT domain accounts are reviewed once a year, not each quarter.
evidence: HR feed configuration; OT domain user export 2026-07-14; jump host account list

implementation_statement: Automated lifecycle for identity provider accounts (create, disable, remove) driven by HR events. The OT domain is not connected to the HR feed; OT disables depend on a ticket from HR.
evidence: IdP provisioning logs; HR termination tickets

implementation_statement: Identity provider accounts unused for 45 days are disabled automatically. The OT domain has no inactivity rule; 11 OT accounts had not logged on in more than 90 days at fieldwork.
evidence: IdP policy; OT domain logon report 2026-07-14

implementation_statement: SCADA application roles separate operator, supervisor, engineer, and administrator functions. OMS roles separate dispatcher, switching author, switching approver, and viewer. Relay access requires the relay engineering role on the gateway access list.
evidence: SCADA role matrix; OMS role catalog (31 roles)

implementation_statement: Traffic between corporate IT and OT must pass through the OT DMZ (historian replica, integration server, file transfer server). Gap: 6 legacy firewall rules allow remote desktop from the corporate server administration subnet directly to the historian and the 2 engineering workstations, bypassing the DMZ (gap 4). Removal is scheduled with the IT/OT firewall redesign.
evidence: IT/OT firewall rule export 2026-07-15; P07 AC-4 results

implementation_statement: Switching orders need an author and a different approver in the OMS module. SCADA database changes are made by engineers and reviewed by the OT Engineering Manager. Gap: the 3 shared SCADA administrator accounts mean changes cannot be tied to a person.
evidence: OMS workflow configuration; SCADA change log

implementation_statement: Least privilege applies to OMS and SCADA roles. Gap: SCADA vendor support uses the shared administrator accounts with full rights on every SCADA server, and privileged access management covers IT and cloud only (gap 5).
evidence: SCADA account list; PAM scope document

implementation_statement: IT administrators use separate privileged accounts through the PAM tool. OT engineers use one OT domain account for both daily work and administration.
evidence: PAM account list; OT domain group membership

implementation_statement: Domain administrator membership in the OT domain is limited to 4 named engineers, but the 3 local shared SCADA administrator accounts sit outside this control.

The identity provider locks accounts after 10 failed attempts for 15 minutes (OMS, jump hosts, cloud). HMI consoles do not lock after failed attempts by design, so operators cannot be locked out during an event; compensated by the DCC physical access control and named accounts (SP 800-82 Rev. 3 tailoring).
evidence: IdP lockout policy; HMI tailoring record

implementation_statement: System use notification banners are shown at the jump hosts, the VPN, the OMS, and HMI logon screens.

Engineering workstations and jump hosts lock after 15 minutes. HMI operator consoles at the DCC do not lock, to keep the grid view available; compensated by the 24x7 staffed, badge-controlled DCC (tailoring decision recorded).
Jump host and OMS sessions end after 8 hours or 30 minutes idle; vendor sessions end at the end time set by the DCC when access is enabled.
evidence: IdP session policy; jump host configuration

implementation_statement: All remote access to OT goes through 2 jump hosts in the OT DMZ with named accounts, MFA through the identity provider, and access enabled per request by the DCC with an end time (CIP-003-9 Attachment 1 Section 6, implemented 2026-03-25). Gap: the relay testing contractor used a cellular modem at Substation H that bypassed the jump hosts and gateway access lists until it was found on 2026-08-19 and disconnected on 2026-08-20 (gap 2). A survey of the other 73 substations for unmanaged remote paths is due 2026-11-30.
evidence: Jump host configuration; DCC access log; P07 AC-17 results; Substation H disconnection record 2026-08-20

implementation_statement: No wireless is permitted inside the OT network at the DCC. Licensed radio and private LTE links to 34 substations use encryption at the radio layer. Gap: no wireless survey of substations; the Substation H modem was not detected for about a year.
Truck tablets are enrolled in mobile device management with encryption, passcode, remote wipe, and an allowlist of OMS mobile, maps, and email.

Personal devices may reach email and chat only through the identity provider with app protection. Contractor-owned laptops may connect to relays at Substations L and H only after a pre-connection review, which is not yet in place (gap 3).
evidence: Conditional access policy; PRC-005 test logs

implementation_statement: Awareness and training policy is part of POL-01 and POL-05 (P06), approved 2026-09-17.

All staff complete the annual CIP awareness module (last 2026-03); office staff also receive monthly phishing simulations (8.6% click rate in 2026-06). Gap: field and DCC staff receive no phishing simulations (gap 15).
Insider threat awareness is a section of the annual module. It does not cover OT-specific insider scenarios (operator misuse, vendor misuse).

OT engineers and system operators receive vendor SCADA training. No role-based security training exists for OT engineers, protection technicians, or dispatchers; a course aligned to SP 800-82 Rev. 3 is planned for 2027-Q1.

Event types logged: jump host sessions, identity provider events, firewall events, SCADA operator actions and alarms (in the SCADA event log), OMS switching actions, cloud control-plane events, EDR events on SCADA servers and HMIs. Gap: substation gateway and field router logs are not collected (gap 6).
Collected logs carry timestamp, source, user, action, and outcome. SCADA operator action logs record console and named user since 2024.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: The MSSP reviews SIEM alerts 24x7 for IT, cloud, and the OT sensors at the DCC, backup DCC, and OT DMZ. The DCC reviews the vendor access log each morning. Gap: no review of SCADA application logs for unexpected commands outside operator actions.
evidence: MSSP monthly report; DCC access log review sign-off

implementation_statement: OT systems take time from 2 GPS-disciplined time servers at the DCC and backup DCC; relays and RTUs use IRIG-B or network time from the same source.

Logs are forwarded to the SIEM and to the write-once log archive in the security and log archive account. SCADA event logs are kept only on the SCADA servers, where the shared administrator accounts could change them.
evidence: Log archive bucket policy; SCADA log location

implementation_statement: SIEM data is kept 1 year hot; the log archive keeps 3 years write-once. Jump host session logs are kept 3 years, longer than the CIP-003-9 compliance evidence retention needs.
Log generation is enabled on all DOP components that support it, except substation gateways and field routers (gap 6).
Controls are assessed each year by the co-sourced internal audit firm with an OT specialist (2026 assessment: P07).

Interconnections with the AMI head-end, CIS, and the 2 transmission owners are covered by contracts and operating agreements. Gap: no written interconnection security terms with the AMI vendor and the 3 carriers.
The POA&M (P07) tracks every weakness with owner and date and is reported to the audit committee each quarter.
Internal authorization equivalent: the Chief Operating Officer (system owner) and the President and CEO accepted continued operation on 2026-09-17 with the POA&M conditions (SSP section 4.2).

Continuous monitoring: EDR and SIEM alerts, monthly vulnerability reports for IT, quarterly SCADA vendor advisory review, and quarterly POA&M review. Gap: no continuous monitoring of the field network and substations.

No penetration test of the OT DMZ or the IT/OT boundary has been done. A test of the OT DMZ and jump hosts from the corporate network, with no active testing of SCADA servers or field devices, is planned for 2027-Q2.

Baseline configurations exist for SCADA servers, HMIs, jump hosts, and firewalls. Gap: no baseline for substation gateways, RTUs, and field devices, and firmware versions are unknown for field devices (gap 8).

SCADA, OMS, and ADMS changes go through the operations change board (weekly) with DCC sign-off. Gap: relay settings changes at Substations L and H by the contractor are logged in PRC-005 records but not in the change board.
evidence: Change board minutes; PRC-005 test logs

implementation_statement: SCADA vendor patches are tested on the backup DCC standby server before the primary. No security impact analysis is done for ADMS changes, including the adaptive load-shedding design (gap 1).
evidence: Patch test records; ADMS project gate checklist

implementation_statement: Only OT engineers can change SCADA servers and databases. The shared administrator accounts weaken attribution (gap 5).
Hardening settings from the SCADA vendor guide are applied to servers and HMIs. Gap: settings are not checked automatically, and 2 HMIs and the historian run an unsupported operating system.
Unneeded services are disabled on SCADA servers and jump hosts. Application allowlisting runs on the 2 engineering workstations and the 4 company relay laptops. Not yet on HMIs.
An OT asset inventory exists for the DCC, backup DCC, OT DMZ, and 74 substations, about 75% complete. Gap: field device firmware versions, radios, and private LTE routers are incomplete (gap 8).
The inventory is updated through the change board for DCC and DMZ systems; field device installs by crews are not fed back to the inventory.
Users cannot install software on HMIs, engineering workstations, or tablets; installs require an OT engineer or IT.
Contingency policy is part of POL-01 and POL-03 (P06); the storm restoration plan and SCADA cyber recovery procedure are the procedures.

The SCADA cyber recovery procedure and backup DCC plan use the BIA (P05) objectives (SCADA RTO 2 hours, OMS RTO 4 hours, switching module RTO 2 hours). Gap: the plan does not cover a ransomware event that reaches both SCADA servers or a malicious change that replicates to the standby.
The plan is coordinated with the storm restoration plan and the transmission owners. Not yet coordinated with the Utility Services client continuity plans.
System operators train on manual operation in the annual storm exercise every May. No training on cyber recovery steps (clean rebuild, integrity checks).

The 2025-11 SCADA restore test took 6 hours against the 2-hour RTO; failover to the backup DCC was last tested in 2024-04 (gap 7). The OMS restore test on 2026-05-19 took 3 hours 10 minutes against the 4-hour RTO.
Cloud backups are copied to a separate backup account in a second region with write-once retention.
The backup DCC at the West Operations Center has 4 HMIs and the hot standby SCADA server. Failover is not tested each year (last 2024-04).
The DCC uses company fiber and licensed radio with private LTE as a diverse path; voice by company radio and satellite phones at both DCCs.

SCADA databases replicate continuously to the hot standby; weekly offline SCADA backups are kept at the backup DCC; OMS uses managed database point-in-time restore with daily copies to the backup account. Gap: relay settings files and OT domain controllers are backed up only inside the OT network.
Backup integrity is tested only in the yearly restore test; offline SCADA backups are not checked weekly.
Recovery uses vendor media and the offline backup. A clean rebuild of a SCADA server has not been rehearsed end to end (gap 7).

baseline: Not in High baseline (added by tailoring for safe OT operation)
implementation_statement: Safe mode for OT (SP 800-82 Rev. 3 overlay): a documented "manual operations" state, in which remote control is disabled, field devices run on local settings, and FLISR is switched off, is planned with the P08 runbook update (2026-11-30).
Identification and authentication are covered by POL-02 and the access control standard (P06).
Users are identified by named accounts in the identity provider and the OT domain. Gap: the 3 shared SCADA administrator accounts.
MFA is required for privileged access to the cloud console, OMS administration, and the jump hosts. Not for OT domain administrator logons made locally at the DCC.
MFA is required for all non-privileged identity provider users, including the OMS, tablets, and the VPN.
Substation gateways permit relay access only from listed addresses. No device authentication for DNP3 field devices (DNP3 Secure Authentication not enabled).
Identifiers are unique except the 3 shared SCADA administrator accounts.

Identity provider password and MFA rules meet POL-02. OT domain passwords expire every 180 days. Gap: the 3 shared administrator passwords never expire and are known to the vendor; relay default passwords were changed at N and E but not verified at L and H.
evidence: Password policy; relay password check list

implementation_statement: Vendor users have named identity provider guest accounts sponsored by a company owner, used for jump host access.
POL-03 (P06) and the low impact Cyber Security Incident response plan (CIP-003-9 Attachment 1 Section 4) set incident response policy.
Incident response training for the security team and MSSP each year. DCC shift supervisors have not been trained on the OT runbook.
The low impact plan was tested by tabletop on 2024-10-08 (within 36 months). No exercise has combined a SCADA intrusion with a storm.
Incident handling follows POL-03 with the MSSP for IT. OT handling depends on the OT engineering team and the insurer panel OT firm; the OT runbook (P08 runbook A) was approved 2026-09-17.
Incidents are tracked in the security case system with timelines.

Reporting duties: E-ISAC for Reportable Cyber Security Incidents (CIP-003-9 Attachment 1 Section 4.2), DOE-417, and EOP-004-4. Gap: DOE-417 cyber criteria were added to the DCC checklist only in the P08 update.
evidence: EOP-004 Operating Plan; P08 notification matrix
regulatory_driver: N22-R01 (CIP-003-9 R2 Att. 1 Sec. 4.2); NERC EOP-004-4 R2; DOE-417

provider_if_inherited: Cyber insurer incident response panel; MSSP
implementation_statement: Assistance from the insurer panel (breach counsel, forensics, OT-capable firm) and the MSSP.
Incident response plan with roles, OT and IT runbooks (P08). Updated 2026-09-17; DCC role cards due 2026-11-30.
Relay and substation equipment maintenance follows PRC-005 intervals with test records.

Nonlocal maintenance by vendors uses the jump hosts with MFA, DCC enablement, and session logging. Gap: the SCADA vendor then uses the shared administrator accounts on the servers, so actions are not tied to a person.
Contractor relay technicians are escorted at Substations N and E. At L and H the contractor works alone with its own laptops, without a pre-connection review (gap 3).
Retired OT drives are wiped and shredded by a certified vendor. Gap: decommissioned relays from L and H were returned to stores without settings erasure.
Removable media are scanned at kiosks at headquarters and the West Operations Center before use on OT. No kiosk at the North, South, and East Operations Centers.
Substation access authorization lists exist. Gap: 2 control house keys at Substations L and H from the former owner are unaccounted for (gap 3).
DCC and backup DCC use badge readers and cameras; substations are fenced and locked with door alarms to the DCC. L and H use the former owner's locks until rekeying.
Door alarms at the 74 substations go to the DCC. Alarms at L and H were connected on 2025-09-15.
Visitor logs at the DCC and backup DCC are kept for 3 years.
UPS and generators support the DCC, backup DCC, and the data room for 72 hours; tested monthly.
Planning policy is part of POL-01 (P06).
This SSP was approved 2026-09-17 and is reviewed yearly.
Staff accept POL-05 acceptable use at hire and each year.

The OT architecture follows a zones and conduits model (SP 800-82 Rev. 3): corporate, OT DMZ, DCC control zone, and substation zones. Gap: the 6 legacy rules (gap 4) and the Substation H modem (gap 2) broke the model.
The security program plan is POL-01 and the FY2027 security plan, approved by the President and CEO.
The Chief Operating Officer is the executive sponsor and CIP Senior Manager (CIP-003-9 R3); the Information Security Manager is the day-to-day lead.
evidence: CIP Senior Manager designation; organization chart

implementation_statement: Risk management strategy and appetite approved by the President and CEO on 2026-09-17 (P01).
Background checks for all staff with DCC, OT, or substation access; contractors attest to equivalent checks.

Termination removes identity provider access automatically and requires key and badge return. Gap: OT domain disables depend on a ticket, and 3 of 25 sampled terminations had OT accounts active more than 5 days after leaving (P07).
evidence: HR exit checklist; P07 PS-4 results

implementation_statement: Transfers trigger an access review by the new manager in the identity provider. OT access is not reviewed on transfer.
Vendor contracts require background checks and confidentiality for staff with access. Only 34 of about 85 vendor contracts have security terms (gap 9).
FIPS 199 categorization of the DOP (this SSP) and CIP-002-5.1a categorization of BES assets (2025-12-09). Gap: the ADMS adaptive load-shedding design was not reviewed under CIP-002 (gap 1).
Yearly risk assessment (P01, 2026-07), with OT scenarios.

IT and cloud are scanned each quarter. OT uses passive vulnerability matching from the OT sensors at the DCC and DMZ plus quarterly SCADA vendor advisory review; no coverage of substations and field devices.
Critical components (SCADA master, jump hosts, relays) are listed in the BIA. No criticality analysis for field devices.
Security requirements are in the SCADA and ADMS contract and the cloud agreement. OT purchases (field devices, radios) have no security requirements or supply chain review (gap 9).
External services (cloud, MSSP, carriers, SCADA vendor support) are listed with owners. Reviews happen only at onboarding (gap 9).
regulatory_driver: N22-R01 (CIP-003-9 R2 Att. 1 Sec. 5.2 and Sec. 6)

implementation_statement: 2 HMI consoles and the historian run an operating system past vendor support; replacement is part of the SCADA upgrade (2027-06). EDR and allowlisting are compensating.
Cloud edge DDoS protection for the OMS mobile endpoints; the OT network has no internet exposure.

Boundary protection: IT/OT firewall with the OT DMZ; substation gateways enforce relay access lists (CIP-003-9 Attachment 1 Section 3.1). Gaps: the 6 legacy rules (gap 4) and the Substation H modem (gap 2, corrected 2026-08-20).
evidence: Firewall and gateway configurations; P07 SC-7 results

control_name: Deny by Default — Allow by Exception
implementation_statement: Deny by default on the OT DMZ firewall and gateways, except the 6 legacy allow rules.
Jump host sessions, OMS, and tablet traffic are encrypted. DNP3 between the SCADA master and substations is not encrypted on fiber links; radio and LTE links are encrypted at the link layer.
OMS databases and backups are encrypted at rest with provider-managed keys.
SCADA vendor patches are reviewed each quarter and applied after testing on the standby server. Field device firmware is not tracked (gap 8).
EDR on SCADA servers, HMIs, engineering workstations, and jump hosts (vendor approved 2025).

Passive OT network sensors at the DCC, backup DCC, and OT DMZ feed the MSSP; IDS signatures on the OT DMZ firewall detect malicious vendor traffic (CIP-003-9 Attachment 1 Section 6.3, since 2026-03-25). Gap: no monitoring at substations or on the field network (gap 6).
evidence: Sensor coverage map; MSSP use cases

implementation_statement: The security team receives E-ISAC, CISA ICS advisories, and SCADA vendor bulletins; quarterly review with OT engineering.
Relay settings are compared with the approved settings file after each PRC-005 test. There is no hash-verified offline copy of settings files, and no integrity check of SCADA database changes.
OMS customer contact data and SCADA historian data follow the records schedule.
A supply chain risk management plan covers IT purchases. OT purchases are not covered (gap 9).
Supply chain controls for the SCADA and ADMS vendor are in the contract. Not for field device makers.
Acquisition strategies (approved suppliers, authorized distributors, firmware verification) for OT devices are planned for 2027-Q1.
The SCADA vendor, cloud provider, AMI vendor, and MSSP provide SOC 2 Type 2 reports reviewed each year (P09). No review for the relay testing contractor or carriers.
Firmware authenticity checks for relays and field devices before installation are planned with SR-5.
